fact: The Ministry of Gender says TNM Mpamba mobile money is disbursing about K6 billion in social cash transfers to over 27,760 beneficiaries in Mangochi District.

During April 2024 to March 2025, 95,520 Social Cash Transfer Programme and 195,520 public works beneficiaries in 10 World Bank-funded districts were enrolled on e-payments and received MWK 4.57 billion and MWK 21.08 billion in e-wallets, per the World Bank aide memoire citing NLGFC.
The deck says the NRB provides beneficiary verification for social protection G2P programmes and maps digital identities to accounts and mobile wallets.

UNICEF Malawi reports that 10 districts have moved to a harmonised e-payment system and pay Social Cash Transfer Programme and Climate Smart Public Works beneficiaries through banks and mobile money operators, e.g. 14,378 in Ntcheu via FDH Bank and 10,070 in Balaka via mobile money.
The guide says mobile money has facilitated social cash transfers and improved the targeting of beneficiaries for social assistance programmes.

Nation Online reports M'Mbelwa District Council now pays Social Cash Transfer Programme beneficiaries' monthly stipends electronically through Kaku Mobile Money Service, replacing cash pay parades, with EU support.
NLGFC's e-payment specialist said Social Cash Transfer and Climate Smart beneficiaries in Dowa are paid digitally, now through TNM Mpamba, with 16,725 and 23,900 beneficiaries.
